key_factors: Turkey's first World Cup since 2002 — the return of the third-place 2002 heroes creates huge motivation
Three injury doubts (Çalhanoğlu, Yıldız, Kadıoğlu) — genuine pre-match XI uncertainty
Arda Güler (Real Madrid) is Turkey's creative heartbeat — Montella's deployment is the key tactical question
Australia missing Riley McGree — their best chance creator — significantly weakens their attack
CBS FanDuel odds: Turkey -145 favourite reflects clear market consensus
reasoning: Turkey ended a 24-year World Cup absence with character — a 1-0 win in Kosovo from Aktürkoğlu's header, then 2-1 over Venezuela in warm-up. Montella's fluid tactical system and the Güler-Aktürkoğlu combination give Turkey real attacking variety. The injury trio (Çalhanoğlu, Yıldız, Kadıoğlu) is the one major risk factor — if all three miss, Turkey are a considerably less potent side. Even so, Australia's creative deficit without McGree means Turkey should have enough to control the match. A 2-1 win feels right: Turkey score twice, Australia pull one back from a dead-ball situation, but Turkey hold on for the three points.

Turkey return to the World Cup stage after 24 years with the quality of Arda Güler and Kerem Aktürkoğlu enough to unlock a disciplined but limited Australia side missing Riley McGree. Even if Çalhanoğlu is managed carefully, Turkey's fluid attacking shape under Montella should find pockets between Australia's wing-backs. Australia will threaten from set-pieces but Turkey's superior technical quality across the squad sees them through to a 2-1 victory.
